one_line: Agent-native furniture discovery, spatial staging, and checkout.
what_it_does: Uses WebMCP tools to search a large furniture catalog, stage authentic items in a room, apply constraints, and prepare checkout.
leverage_rationale: Structured catalog, spatial, and checkout operations are substantially more reliable than an agent inferring furniture UI, though the packet provides no live video proof.
leverage_evidence: Pitch describes search across 14,000+ items and room-fit checkout.
Devpost screenshot visibly presents the project packaging and embedded demo preview.
execution_rationale: The packaging is coherent and the screenshot preview shows a plausible furniture copilot flow, but no submitted frame sheet or transcript provides end-to-end verification.
execution_evidence: Screenshot shows coherent Devpost presentation and demo media.
impact_rationale: Furniture shoppers have a concrete visualization and selection problem, and authentic catalog staging plus constraints directly address it.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies room visualization, dimensions, budget, and checkout use cases.
creativity_rationale: The combination of multimodal room fitting, non-hallucinatory catalog assets, and agent-mediated commerce is a fresh synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Zero-hallucination staging and spatial commerce are central claims.
usability_note: Promising conversational-to-checkout flow; live usability is not fully evidenced.
red_flags: No video frame sheets or transcript; end-to-end claims are thinly evidenced.
standouts: Authentic catalog geometry and room-fit checkout concept.
advance_reason: Strong commerce use case and meaningful WebMCP delta, despite limited execution evidence.

one_line: Parametric 3D pottery design with deterministic printable templates.
what_it_does: Lets an agent and human edit parametric vessel geometry while the app deterministically generates reversible, multi-page clay templates.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP/shared state makes agent complexity and human precision complementary; deterministic export is difficult to reproduce with generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes paired ChatGPT/browser state synced over WebSocket.
Transcript demonstrates agent changes arriving in the editor and undo/redo.
execution_rationale: The video transcript and frame sheets establish a coherent editor, agent connection, parameter changes, and reversible deterministic output; some edge coverage is absent.
execution_evidence: Transcript describes parameter update, synced browser state, and undo/redo.
Devpost describes exported multi-page PDF templates.
impact_rationale: Potters have a specific costly failure mode—misaligned templates—and this directly reduces wasted studio work.
impact_evidence: Devpost identifies repeated AI template failures and studio rework.
Product outputs printable templates true to the designed shape.
creativity_rationale: The human-agent parametric pottery workflow and deterministic physical-template bridge are unusually memorable and deeply pursued.
creativity_evidence: Agent handles exploration while deterministic geometry handles fabrication.
Paired browser model and reversible command history are distinctive.
usability_note: Human-editable parameters, pairing, and undo/redo support a practical workflow.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage with strong demonstrated execution and a clear real audience.

one_line: A user-controlled passport for personalized physical-world experiences.
what_it_does: Exposes personal and place context through a digital passport so agents can tailor real-world experiences, including adaptive fitness.
leverage_rationale: Structured, user-approved personal/place context can make personalization more reliable than an agent guessing from a generic page, but the live demo is dead.
leverage_evidence: Pitch centers on a digital passport and approved scope.
Devpost text names Adaptive Gym and Passport WebMCP.
execution_rationale: The concept and packaging are understandable, but the reported dead demo and absence of video make the central workflow unverified.
execution_evidence: Screenshot is packaging evidence only; no frame sheets or transcript.
impact_rationale: Personalized fitness and place-aware experiences address real accessibility and wellness needs, though the demonstrated solution is unclear.
impact_evidence: Devpost describes personalized Pilates/rehabilitation motivation and Adaptive Gym.
creativity_rationale: A consented passport making physical places agent-readable is an original interaction model with meaningful ambition.
creativity_evidence: User-controlled digital passport and approved-scope framing.
usability_note: Potentially useful, but the dead demo prevents judging actual interaction quality.
standouts: Consent and approved-scope framing for real-world personalization.
advance_reason: Interesting concept but insufficient execution evidence and a dead demo.

one_line: Agent-readable service marketplace with preview and human-authorized purchasing.
what_it_does: Provides fixed WebMCP tools for intent search, exact service contracts, dry-run previews, and guarded prepaid purchases.
leverage_rationale: Structured contracts, dry-run receipts, bounded tools, and server-side purchase guards materially improve agent reliability and preserve a human payment boundary.
leverage_evidence: Four page-scoped tools expose discovery, contract inspection, preview, and purchase.
Purchase authority remains server-side and the person authorizes buying.
execution_rationale: The description is unusually specific about workflow states, guards, scope, and regression coverage; no video reduces certainty about runtime behavior.
execution_evidence: Devpost details exact tool behavior, mutation guards, and synthetic preview flow.
impact_rationale: Agents need safe discovery and contract inspection for paid services, and users benefit from explicit preview and payment boundaries.
impact_evidence: Product targets agent marketplace discovery and safe purchase authorization.
Preview stops before payment in the challenge demo.
creativity_rationale: The contract-first marketplace and free dry-run receipt are a thoughtful, original application of agent-native commerce.
creativity_evidence: Fixed tool surface grows with inventory without one tool per service.
Human retains preview and purchase decisions.
usability_note: Clear separation between agent discovery and human authorization supports trust.
red_flags: No video transcript or submitted frame evidence.
standouts: Strong safety boundary and precise service contracts.
advance_reason: A coherent, safety-conscious agent marketplace with meaningful WebMCP leverage.

one_line: Agent-queryable visualization and SQL exploration for company AI-transformation scores.
what_it_does: Combines charts, in-browser DuckDB SQL, sector/company views, and linked reports for a 0–100 AI transformation dataset.
leverage_rationale: Structured query and chart generation reduce friction for analytical questions, though a capable agent could achieve much of this through ordinary UI interaction.
leverage_evidence: Devpost describes WebMCP driving SQL/query surface.
25-chart gallery, DuckDB, and report links are specified.
execution_rationale: The scope is coherent and the packet includes multiple frame sheets, but no transcript and no direct end-to-end claim beyond the described demo.
execution_evidence: Devpost names gallery, SQL, heatmap, radar, and company report flows.
impact_rationale: Analysts and investors can ask cross-company and sector questions more naturally than scrolling a catalog, with reports linked for context.
impact_evidence: Specific healthcare/industrials ranking use cases are described.
creativity_rationale: It is a competent and useful synthesis of financial/business scoring, SQL, charts, and agent querying, with moderate novelty.
creativity_evidence: Agent-driven query-to-chart surface over a frozen S&P 500 snapshot.
usability_note: Multiple analytical views and linked reports suggest a useful exploratory workflow.
red_flags: Snapshot is frozen and season remains open, which limits freshness outside the challenge.
standouts: Query-to-chart workflow over a concrete business dataset.
advance_reason: Solid, credible analytical product with meaningful agent-query improvement.

one_line: A browser canvas that grows purpose-built interfaces and APIs from agent requests.
what_it_does: Agents compose tables, kanban boards, forms, charts, notes, and checklists; human edits share a command log and forms can create persistent WebMCP tools.
leverage_rationale: The product's core value is shared live state plus dynamic tool creation: the agent extends both the interface and its own future API, beyond ordinary UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Devpost describes 15 tools, shared command log, stale-state detection, and undo.
Generated form schemas register persistent new WebMCP tools across reloads.
execution_rationale: The architecture and workflow are coherent and ambitious, with frame sheets supporting a real product surface; dynamic generation edge cases are not fully evidenced.
execution_evidence: Description specifies six widgets, command log, undo, and persistent tools.
impact_rationale: Teams and individuals can quickly create task-specific software without committing to a fixed app, while retaining direct manipulation.
impact_evidence: Examples include wedding planning, job tracking, and health logging.
Human-agent shared artifact is directly useful.
creativity_rationale: The concept of software and API growing together from a goal, with schemas derived from generated forms, is highly original and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Dynamic WebMCP tool creation from user-created form fields.
One command log unifies agent and human edits.
usability_note: Direct manipulation and goal-first generation are strong usability choices, though generated-app quality can vary.
red_flags: No transcript; dynamic tool lifecycle is described more than directly verified.
standouts: Software/API co-evolution and shared command history.
advance_reason: Outstanding WebMCP-native concept with broad utility and strong originality.

one_line: SRE incident workbench with agent investigation and explicit operator approval.
what_it_does: Unifies incident telemetry, diagnostics, staged rollback, postmortem drafting, and guarded execution behind a visible human approval gate.
leverage_rationale: Typed incident tools and approval-bound execution make agent investigation precise while preserving accountable control; generic UI driving is riskier and less reliable.
leverage_evidence: Seven typed tools cover detect through recovery.
No approval tool exists; execution revalidates staged and UI-approved mitigation IDs.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a complete, internally consistent simulated incident lifecycle with safety checks, though video evidence is absent.
execution_evidence: Devpost details metrics, rollback, approval, replay protection, and recovery outcomes.
impact_rationale: Incident response is a high-value operational problem, and the product directly addresses the tension between fast agent investigation and accountable production action.
impact_evidence: Concrete latency/error regression and recovery scenario.
Explicit approval boundary prevents unsafe execution.
creativity_rationale: The approval boundary as a first-class product primitive and full incident lifecycle are a strong, thoughtful agent-native interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agent can stage but cannot self-approve mitigation.
Evidence timeline and replay protection are integrated.
usability_note: Centralized context and visible approval state fit operator workflows.
red_flags: Simulated incident rather than live production integration.
standouts: Strong safety architecture and complete response flow.

one_line: Behavioral trust layer that compares WebMCP declarations with observed effects.
what_it_does: Classifies declared tool contracts, observes network/storage/navigation effects, compares behavior, and decides whether to allow or flag execution.
leverage_rationale: It addresses a WebMCP-specific trust gap that ordinary browser automation does not solve: verifying a tool's behavior against its declared contract.
leverage_evidence: Devpost describes Declare → Classify → Observe → Compare → Decide.
Attack demo attempts payment-like activity despite harmless tool description.
execution_rationale: The security model and adversarial example are coherent, but no transcript and limited visible evidence constrain confidence in completeness.
execution_evidence: Description names observed effect classes and comparison flow.
impact_rationale: Misrepresented agent tools create a serious safety problem; behavioral verification could protect users across agent-native sites.
impact_evidence: Addresses trust in tool declarations, a stated WebMCP concern.
creativity_rationale: Turning WebMCP declarations into behaviorally testable contracts is a novel and important security interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Tool lies by declaring harmless behavior while mutating payment state and navigating.
Browser-visible effects are compared with declared intent.
usability_note: Trust decisions could be valuable, but false-positive handling and operator UX are not fully evidenced.
red_flags: Devpost states the project began before the hackathon as a different project; origin is treated as pre-existing with challenge pivot.
standouts: Directly tackles a fundamental WebMCP trust boundary.
advance_reason: Important, original WebMCP security problem with a concrete adversarial demonstration.

one_line: Chrome extension that installs curated WebMCP adapters on legacy websites.
what_it_does: Uses versioned adapters and integrity checks to expose structured tools for ESPN Fantasy, Domino's, Hacker News, Wikipedia, and other unsupported sites.
leverage_rationale: Adapters replace brittle screenshot/selector control with structured site-specific tools and show large reliability gains, though curation is required.
leverage_evidence: Devpost reports 16/16 intended ESPN picks versus 3/16 with ordinary browser control.
Extension registers tools through document.modelContext and verifies SHA-256 adapter sources.
execution_rationale: The architecture, supported sites, update/integrity model, and quantitative comparison form a coherent product story; no transcript limits observation.
execution_evidence: Description details extension, runtime, registry, versioning, and integrity checks.
impact_rationale: Many useful sites lack agent interfaces; a practical adapter layer can make everyday tasks more reliable without requiring site owners to rebuild them.
impact_evidence: Multiple concrete adapters across sports, food, news, and reference.
Reported improvement in fantasy draft completion.
creativity_rationale: The curated adapter marketplace/registry approach is a scalable and memorable bridge from the old web to WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Extension teaches unsupported sites to speak WebMCP.
Integrity-verified isolated adapters are a thoughtful design.
usability_note: Sideloadable extension and curated adapters promise a simple user experience, subject to compatibility maintenance.
red_flags: Adapter coverage depends on ongoing curation and site changes.
standouts: Concrete reliability comparison and integrity-aware adapter registry.
advance_reason: Strong practical WebMCP leverage with a credible bridge for the existing web.

one_line: Browser-local full-stack website builder operated through WebMCP.
what_it_does: Lets an agent build frontend pages, compile Rust backend blocks, stock shops, preview live changes, undo generations, and export a site locally.
leverage_rationale: Typed page-specific build, compile, publish, rollback, and export capabilities are central to the product and far more reliable than generic browser clicking.
leverage_evidence: Devpost describes tools for frontend, backend compilation, products, undo, and export.
All runs in a browser service worker with no external provider.
execution_rationale: The scope is ambitious and internally coherent, but the packet lacks transcript and the central full-stack workflow is not directly verified by frames here.
execution_evidence: Description specifies live preview, Rust compilation, rollback, export, and local execution.
impact_rationale: Small teams and individuals can produce deployable sites without toolchain setup, provider accounts, or recurring platform fees.
impact_evidence: Concrete build, backend, shop, rollback, and export workflow.
No external providers or extra costs is a clear user benefit.
creativity_rationale: A browser-local full-stack compiler and website builder controlled through WebMCP is highly ambitious and unusual.
creativity_evidence: Rust backend blocks compile inside the browser service worker.
Agent builds a complete website from one page and exports it.
usability_note: One-URL workflow and rollback are appealing, but login and complex compilation may add friction.
red_flags: Very broad scope with no transcript; backend compilation and export require stronger direct evidence.
advance_reason: Ambitious and highly WebMCP-native developer product with credible user value.
